source_text: Nam quod addidit dicens: prouidentia dei patris, quid aliud ambiuit Iesu Christo nominato. cuius se dicit apostolum, et deo patre, cuius prouidentia missum se dicit a filio, nisi ut spiritum sanctum ipsum esse tertium crederemus? sic enim scribit: Manichaeus apostolus Iesu Christi prouidentia dei patris. spiritus sanctus nominatus non est, qui maxime debuit ab eo nominari, qui nobis apostolatum suum paracleti promissione commendat, ut euangelica auctoritate inperitos premat. quod cum a uobis quaeritur, respondetis utique Manichaeo apostolo nominato sanctum spiritum paracletum nominari, quia in ipso uenire dignatus est. quaero ergo, sicut superius dicebam, quare exhorreatis, cum dicit catholica eum, in quo uenit diuina sapientia, natum esse de uirgine, cum uos eum, in quo spiritum sanctum uenisse praedicatis, natum de femina uiro mixta nihil horreatis. quid ergo aliud suspicer nescio, nisi quia iste Manichaeus, qui per Christi nomen ad inperitorum animos aditum quaerit, pro ipso Christo se coli uoluit. hoc unde coniciam, breuiter dicam. cum saepe. a uobis quaererem illo tempore. quo uos audiebam, quae causa. esset, quod pascha domini plerumque nulla, interdum a paucis tepidissima celebritate frequentaretis nullis uigiliis, nullo prolixiore ieiunio indicto auditoribus, nullo denique festiuiore adparatu, cum bema uestrum. id est diem, quo Manichaeus occisus est, quinque gradibus instructo tribunali et pretiosis linteis adornato atque in promptu posito et obiecto adorantibus magnis honoribus prosequamini: hoc ergo cum quaererem, respondebatur eius diem passionis celebrandum esse, qui uere passus esset; Christum autem, qui natus non esset, neque ueram, sed simulatam carnem humanis oculis ostendisset, non pertulisse, sed finxisse passionem. quis non gemescat homines. qui se christianos dici uolunt, timere, ne polluatur ueritas de uirginis utero, et de mendacio non timere ? sed ut ad rem redeam, quis non suspicetur, cum diligenter adtenderit, ideo negari a Manichaeo Christum natum esse de femina et humanum corpus habuisse, ne passio eius, quod totius iam orbis festissimum tempus est. ab eis, qui sibi credidissent, celebraretur et non tanta deuotione diem mortis suae desiderata sollemnitas honoraret? hoc enim nobis erat in illa bematis celebritate gratissimum, quod pro pascha frequentabatur, quoniam uehementius desiderabamus illum diem festum subtracto alio, qui solebat esse dulcissimus.
thought_title: Mani's self-presentation and the Bema festival
orientation: Augustine is addressing the Manichaeans, arguing that Mani's opening self-description as 'apostle of Jesus Christ by the providence of God the Father' is a ploy to make himself worshipped in place of Christ.
pass_a_gloss: For what he added, saying: by the providence of God the Father, what else did he seek, when Jesus Christ had been named, whose apostle he says he is, and God the Father, by whose providence he says he was sent by the Son, except that we should believe that the Holy Spirit himself is the third? For he writes thus: Mani, apostle of Jesus Christ by the providence of God the Father. The Holy Spirit is not named, who especially ought to have been named by him, who commends his apostleship to us by the promise of the Paraclete, so that he may press down the inexperienced with gospel authority. When this is asked of you, you answer that when Mani the apostle is named, the Holy Spirit the Paraclete is named, because he deigned to come in him. Therefore I ask, as I was saying above, why you shudder when the Catholic Church says that he, in whom divine Wisdom came, was born of a virgin, while you do not shudder at all that he, in whom you proclaim the Holy Spirit came, was born of a woman mixed with a man. Therefore I do not know what else to suspect, except that this Mani, who seeks access to the minds of the inexperienced through the name of Christ, wanted himself to be worshipped in place of Christ himself. From what I may infer this, I will say briefly. When I often asked you at that time, when I was listening to you, what the reason was, that you attended the Lord's Passover mostly with no celebration, sometimes with a very lukewarm celebration by a few, with no vigils, no longer fast enjoined upon the hearers, no more festive preparation, while you honor your Bema festival, that is, the day on which Mani was killed, with a tribunal furnished with five steps and adorned with precious linens and placed in view and set before the worshippers with great honors: therefore when I asked this, it was answered that the day of his passion ought to be celebrated, who truly suffered; but Christ, who had not been born, and had shown not true but feigned flesh to human eyes, had not endured, but had feigned his passion. Who would not groan at men who want themselves to be called Christians, fearing that truth be polluted from a virgin's womb, and not fearing from a lie? But to return to the matter, who would not suspect, when he has attended carefully, that for this reason Christ is denied by Mani to have been born of a woman and to have had a human body, lest his passion, which is now the most festive time of the whole world, be celebrated by those who had believed him, and the desired solemnity not honor the day of his death with so great devotion? For this was most pleasing to us in that celebration of the Bema festival, that it was attended in place of the Passover, since we desired more vehemently that festal day when the other, which used to be most sweet, had been taken away.

choices.english: by the providence of God the Father
choices.why: Literal rendering of the ablative of means; keeps the phrase as Mani's self-description rather than a theological gloss.
rejected: through the providence of God the Father

choices.why: Literal sense of those lacking experience or knowledge; Augustine uses it for those easily deceived.
Glossary requires 'Bema festival' for bema; 'uestrum' is rendered as 'your' to keep the possessive force.
Literal rendering of 'simulatam' as 'feigned' preserves the accusation that Christ's flesh was pretended, not real.

choices.english: with a tribunal furnished with five steps
choices.why: Literal rendering of the ablative absolute; 'instructo' as 'furnished' keeps the sense of equipped or arranged.
rejected: with a tribunal built with five steps
with a platform of five steps

choices.term: pro ipso Christo se coli uoluit
choices.english: wanted himself to be worshipped in place of Christ himself
choices.why: Literal rendering of 'pro ipso Christo' as 'in place of Christ himself' preserves the substitutionary sense.
rejected: wanted himself worshipped instead of Christ
wanted to be worshipped as Christ

pass_b_english: For when he added the words “by the providence of God the Father,” what else was he aiming at, after naming Jesus Christ—whose apostle he calls himself—and God the Father, by whose providence he says he was sent by the Son, than to make us believe that he himself is the third person, the Holy Spirit? This is how he writes: “Mani, apostle of Jesus Christ by the providence of God the Father.” The Holy Spirit is not named, though he above all ought to have been named by the man who commends his apostleship to us by the promise of the Paraclete, so that he may press down the inexperienced with the authority of the gospel. When you are asked about this, you answer that when Mani is named as apostle, the Holy Spirit, the Paraclete, is named, because he deigned to come in him. So I ask, as I was saying above, why you shudder when the Catholic Church says that the one in whom divine Wisdom came was born of a virgin, while you feel no shudder at all that the one in whom you proclaim the Holy Spirit came was born from a woman joined with a man. What else I should suspect, I do not know, except that this Mani, who seeks access to the minds of the inexperienced through the name of Christ, wanted himself to be worshipped in place of Christ himself. I will say briefly how I infer this. When I often asked you, in the time when I was listening to you, what the reason was that you generally observed the Lord’s Passover with no celebration at all, or sometimes with a very lukewarm one from a few people—with no vigils, no longer fast enjoined on the hearers, no more festive display—while you honor your Bema festival, that is, the day on which Mani was killed, with great honors, with a tribunal furnished with five steps and adorned with costly linens, set out in full view and presented to those who worship: when I asked this, the answer was that the day of the passion of the one who truly suffered should be celebrated; but Christ, who was not born and showed not true but feigned flesh to human eyes, did not undergo but feigned his passion. Who would not groan at men who want to be called Christians, who fear that truth may be polluted from a virgin’s womb, and do not fear pollution from a lie? But to return to the matter: who would not suspect, if he paid careful attention, that Mani denied that Christ was born of a woman and had a human body for this reason—so that his passion, which is now the most festive season of the whole world, would not be celebrated by those who had believed Mani, and so that the longed-for solemnity of his own death day would be honored with such great devotion? For this was what pleased us most in that Bema festival celebration: it was observed in place of the Passover, because we desired that feast day more intensely when the other, which used to be sweetest, had been taken away.

last_rejected.quote: than to make us believe that he himself is the third person, the Holy Spirit?
last_rejected.why: Source says 'believe the third' (i.e., the third person); English adds 'person' but omits 'tertium' as 'the third' in sequence.
last_rejected.fix: than to make us believe that he is the third, the Holy Spirit?
last_rejected.ruling: 'tertium' with no noun, in Trinitarian context, naturally means 'third person'; English correctly supplies it.

last_rejected.quote: by whose providence he says he was sent by the Son
last_rejected.source_quote: et deo patre, cuius prouidentia missum se dicit a filio
last_rejected.why: Latin says 'a filio' (by the Son), but 'missum...a filio' means 'sent by the Son,' not 'sent by the Father.' The agency is confused: Mani claims to be sent by the Son, not that the Father sent him by the Son's action.
last_rejected.fix: by whose providence he says the Son sent him
last_rejected.ruling: Latin 'missum se dicit a filio' = 'he says he was sent by the Son'; English matches exactly. No error.

last_rejected.quote: press down the inexperienced with the authority of the gospel
last_rejected.why: 'premat' here means 'overwhelm/tyrannize/oppress,' not 'press down' in a neutral sense. The context is manipulative: Mani uses gospel authority to overpower the inexperienced.
last_rejected.fix: so that he may overwhelm the inexperienced with gospel authority
last_rejected.ruling: 'Press down' is valid for 'premat'; 'overwhelm/oppress' is nuance, not a changed meaning.

last_rejected.quote: For this was what pleased us most in that Bema festival celebration: it was observed in place of the Passover, because we desired that feast day more intensely when the other, which used to be sweetest, had been taken away.
last_rejected.source_quote: hoc enim nobis erat in illa bematis celebritate gratissimum, quod pro pascha frequentabatur, quoniam uehementius desiderabamus illum diem festum subtracto alio, qui solebat esse dulcissimus
last_rejected.why: The English 'us/we' hides that Augustine is speaking as a former Manichaean hearer, using first-person from inside that experience. The shift to 'us' is jarring without marking this as Augustine's past self.
last_rejected.fix: For this was what pleased us most... we desired that feast day more intensely (as I then felt)
last_rejected.ruling: 'us/we' faithfully renders 'nobis'; context already marks Augustine's past Manichaean experience. No meaning lost.

problems.quote: would not be celebrated by those who had believed him
problems.why: sibi is Mani, set against eius (Christ’s passion). “him” reads as Christ.
problems.fix: would not be celebrated by those who had believed Mani
problems.ruling: "sibi" refers to Mani (reflexive), but "believed him" after "his passion" (Christ's) reads as Christ; reader misled about whom they believed.

problems.quote: the day of his passion should be celebrated who truly suffered
problems.source_quote: eius diem passionis celebrandum esse, qui uere passus esset
problems.why: Garbled word order: the day of passion of the one who truly suffered should be celebrated; reads as unclear.
problems.fix: the passion-day of the one who truly suffered should be celebrated
problems.ruling: “eius…qui uere passus esset” is the one who truly suffered; English leaves “who” with no clear person.

edits.old: the day of his passion should be celebrated who truly suffered
edits.new: the day of the passion of the one who truly suffered should be celebrated

edits.old: would not be celebrated by those who had believed him
edits.new: would not be celebrated by those who had believed Mani

fixed: agency: 'him' changed to 'Mani' because sibi is Mani versus eius for Christ's passion
mistranslation: word order fixed so qui uere passus esset modifies the one whose day is celebrated

last_rejected.quote: and so that the longed-for solemnity of his own death day would be honored with such great devotion
last_rejected.source_quote: et non tanta deuotione diem mortis suae desiderata sollemnitas honoraret
last_rejected.why: The solemnity is the subject that honors the day of his death; English makes that day’s solemnity the thing honored.
last_rejected.fix: and so that the solemnity they longed for would honor the day of his own death with such great devotion
last_rejected.ruling: English 'the longed-for solemnity of his own death day would be honored' renders 'diem mortis suae desiderata sollemnitas honoraret' within normal range; the sense (honoring his death day with a desired solemnity) is preserved.

last_rejected.quote: he above all ought to have been named by the man who commends his apostleship to us by the promise of the Paraclete
last_rejected.source_quote: qui maxime debuit ab eo nominari, qui nobis apostolatum suum paracleti promissione commendat
last_rejected.why: Accurate overall, but 'ambiuit' sense (aiming/canvassing) fine. No error here; retained only as check.
last_rejected.ruling: Matches qui maxime debuit ab eo nominari, qui apostolatum suum paracleti promissione commendat; no meaning lost.
